## Question 1 [5]{.marks}

Separating variables, $y^{-2} \, \mathrm{d}y = x \, \mathrm{d}x$, so $-y^{-1} = \frac{x^2}{2} + C$. [2]{.marks}

The initial condition $y(0) = 1$ gives $C = -1$, so
$$
y(x) = \frac{2}{2 - x^2}.
$$ [2]{.marks}

The solution blows up at $x = \pm\sqrt{2}$, so it exists on $(-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2})$. [1]{.marks}

::: {.marking}
Accept any equivalent form of the solution. The interval mark needs both end points.
:::

## Question 2 [5]{.marks}

(a) The integrating factor is $\mathrm{e}^{2t}$, so $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\mathrm{e}^{2t} x\right) = \mathrm{e}^{t}$. [1]{.marks}

    Integrating gives
    $$
    x(t) = \mathrm{e}^{-t} + C \, \mathrm{e}^{-2t}.
    $$ [2]{.marks}

(b) Both terms decay, so every solution tends to $0$ as $t \to \infty$ (like $\mathrm{e}^{-t}$). [2]{.marks}
